cli.input: --input selects the event timeline only; default /app/data/event_timeline.json

description: Output contract for the incident-correlation engine. Shapes, paths, field lists and sort orders only; no derivation rule lives here.

incident_chains.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline
incident_chains.sort: descending by severity, then ascending by first_ts, then chain_id; hosts in first-seen order; actions ascending

summary.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline

field_notes.event_count: events in the timeline handed to --input
field_notes.session_count: sessions the events fall into once the governed gap is applied
field_notes.chain_candidate_count: candidate chains formed before the severity floor and the pivot are applied
field_notes.incident_chain_count: chains reported in incident_chains.json, so the candidates that cleared both
field_notes.truncated_chain_count: reported chains that ran past the host cap and were cut
field_notes.queued_count: rows in triage_queue.jsonl, both reasons together
field_notes.max_severity: the greatest severity among the REPORTED chains, so a candidate that fell below the floor does not raise it; 0 when nothing is reported

triage_queue.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, trailing newline
triage_queue.sort: descending by severity, then ascending by chain_id then host

event_timeline.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline

sensor_registry.note: applied during the timeline recovery, not re-read at correlation time

units.severity: integer points fixed per action by the response board
units.timestamps: integer seconds on the reference clock
